text:
Jordan: Hey @Maria and @Support Lead — Snowplow (tenant: snowplow-prod) reported a burst of 429s and elevated latency on Dedicated pool dp-8. They say it began after switching to long-context chat (~20k tokens). They see frequent 'kv_evict' entries and CPU spikes on serving nodes.

Maria: On it. Any repro steps from the customer? What model and sequence length distribution?

Jordan: Model: open-rw-13b. Workload: chat completions with heavy prefix reuse. Many requests have 12k-18k contexts and multiple concurrent sessions coming from the same org bot. Customer provided sample request id r-9f12a3 and this curl repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -d '{"model":"open-rw-13b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<12k prefix>"},{"role":"user","content":"gen long"}], "max_tokens":1024}'
```

SRE-Bot: ALERT: dp-8 | KV_CACHE_EVICT_RATE spike | avg_evictions=154/s | mem_frag=0.72 | 429_rate=12/min (since 2401123400)

Tim: I've pulled logs — I see evict traces and slab reorg thrashing. Example: 
```
[2026-07-15T03:10:21Z] INFO kvcache: evicting 2048 keys, reason=fragmentation
[2026-07-15T03:10:21Z] WARN runtime: serve_latency=780ms tokens=220
[2026-07-15T03:10:22Z] ERROR http: 429 tenant=snowplow-prod req=r-9f12a3
```

Devon: That pattern smells like fragmentation + large KV entries from long sessions. Could also be a mix of very long hot keys and many short churny sessions. Any slab-level metrics? p99 slab free seems low.

Maria: Requesting heap/pprof dumps and kvstats for pool dp-8. Also ask the customer to hit /internal/debug/sessions for the tenant. Ask them to repro during our tailing window.

Jordan: Asked customer to run repro at 15:30 PT with a small wrapper to fire 3 parallel sessions: 
```
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @longctx.json &
done
wait
```

OpsBot: ACTION: Created incident INC-2401123 and attached dp-8 metrics dashboard. Link: https://console.redwood/internal/inc/INC-2401123

Tim: Quick mitigation options: increase kv_cache_max_entries for snowplow on dp-8 from 120k -> 200k and enable aggressive prefix caching for that tenant. Caveat: increases overall memory usage and could worsen fragmentation. Safer: enforce a router-side soft-limit on concurrent long-context sessions (reduce from 3 -> 2) to reduce eviction pressure.

Support Lead: Try soft throttling first while we gather diagnostics. Maria, coordinate the config change and a rollback plan. Notify Sales/CS.

Maria: Rolling a canary config change to limit long-context concurrency to 2 for the tenant and enable prefix_kvcaching=true. Canary on 2 nodes first.

[OpsBot]: config apply dp-8:route-policy:snowplow -> {"concurrency_limit_longctx":2, "prefix_kvcaching":true}

Tim: Also collect heap snapshots and kvstats: 
- node dp-8-03: curl http://dp-8-03.internal:9000/debug/pprof/heap > heap-03.pb 
- run `redwood-admin kvstats --pool dp-8 --tenant snowplow-prod > kvstats.txt`

Devon: Watch metrics 'kvcache_fragmentation_ratio' and per-slab free_chunks. If fragmentation_ratio > 0.6, we'll plan a rolling restart with defrag enabled and increase slab sizes to reduce reallocation churn.

Jordan: Customer ran the 3-parallel repro during our window. After soft throttle was applied they saw 429s drop and median latency improved to ~220ms from ~680ms. Occasional evict warnings persisted but no sustained 429 storm.

Maria: Collected heap + kvstats, excerpts below: 
```
kvcache.total_entries=118432
kvcache.evictions_1m=162
kvcache.fragmentation_ratio=0.71
slab.0.free_chunks=48
slab.1.free_chunks=3
```

Tim: fragmentation_ratio 0.71 — confirms fragmentation-driven evictions. Next: schedule rolling restart with `--kv-defrag=true` and bump `kv_initial_slab_mb` for dp-8 by ~25% to reduce immediate reallocation. Do during low-traffic window. Also recommend customer reduce max_tokens where feasible and trim older prefixes from session histories.

Support Lead: Approved defrag restart tonight at 02:00 UTC. Maria, update incident with rollback steps and a customer-facing impact note.

Maria: Draft message to customer: "We'll perform a rolling maintenance (no downtime expected) to defragment the KV cache and apply tuning. During the window you may see a few short 429s as nodes restart. Please pause large batch replays during this hour." :white_check_mark: 

Jordan: Post-maintenance plan: keep soft throttle at 2 for 48h and monitor evict_rate. If evictions remain >50/s, consider resizing the pool or migrating the tenant to a larger pool (dp-9).

Devon: Add alert: if kvcache.fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 AND evictions_1m > 100 => page oncall.

SRE-Bot: NOTE: incident INC-2401123 updated: maintenance scheduled 2401126800 -> 2401128600 UTC. Monitors created.

Tim: TL;DR — Root cause: KV slab fragmentation from mixed long-context large entries + high concurrency from a single tenant. Short-term: router soft throttle + prefix caching. Medium-term: rolling defrag restarts + slab resizing. Long-term: recommend dedicated larger pool or workload changes (shorter prefixes, lower max_tokens).

Support Lead: Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread after maintenance. :thumbsup:
